Arjun Sen
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Akhilesh Kumar Saxena, counsel for the applicant
 Shri Kshitij Vyas, P.L. for State.

Order 
This first bail application under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 439 of Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the applicant Arjun Sen for grant of regular bail in relation to Crime/FIR No.129/2024 registered at Police Station Mo.Badodiya, District Shajapur (M.P.) for commission of offence under Sections 363, 366(A) and 376(2)(n) of IPC and sec.5/6 of POCSO Act.

The applicant is in jail since 22.06.2024.
2.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has not committed any offence as alleged against him.
Even in the statement of prosecutrix recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C., she has not made any allegation against him.
Applicant is in jail since 22.6.2024.
Investigation is completed, chargesheet has been filed and conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time.
Therefore, learned counsel prays for allowing the application for grant of bail.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:429 2 MCRC-55471-2024
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposed the prayer.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
5.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the period of custody and that investigation is completed, chargesheet has been filed and the applicant is not required for further custodial interrogation , this Court is inclined to grant benefit of bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, bail application is allowed.
